Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Systems Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as it may be interpreted as a disconnect. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Systems' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Robert Kline, Chief Medical Officer; and David Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency across our 180-hospital footprint spanning 25 states.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on five key areas: robust same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter; strong net patient revenue expansion; disciplined capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion; clear operating margin guidance for the coming periods; and forward-looking capital expenditure plans to fuel sustainable growth.

Same-facility admissions rose 4.5% year-over-year, accelerating from prior quarters, with patient days up 5.2%, reflecting higher acuity and effective length of stay management. Net patient revenue hit $2.85 billion, growing 8.7% year-over-year and 2.3% sequentially, driven by volume, case mix, and payer improvements. We invested $285 million in capital expenditures, prioritizing high-return modernization and Sunbelt expansions. For margins, we're guiding to 9.5% to 10% in the next quarter and 10% to 10.8% for the full year. And our CapEx guidance supports ongoing investments at $380 to $410 million for Q4 and $1.65 to $1.75 billion next year.

These results highlight our resilience amid reimbursement pressures and labor challenges, with broad-based strength in orthopedics, cardiology, and Sunbelt markets. Now, I’ll turn the call over to Jennifer to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $2.85 billion, an increase of 8.7% compared to the same period last year and up 2.3% from the prior quarter. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, improved payer mix, and a favorable shift toward higher-acuity cases.

Let me break down our net patient revenue performance, which remains the cornerstone of our financial health in this dynamic sector. For the quarter ended June 30, 2024, net patient revenue totaled $2.85 billion, reflecting that year-over-year growth of 8.7% and sequential quarter-over-quarter growth of 2.3% from the prior quarter's $2.78 billion. On a full-year basis through the first half, we've reached about $5.7 billion, positioning us for strong full-year momentum. These results outperformed our initial guidance and align with the industry's post-pandemic rebound, though tempered by ongoing reimbursement headwinds from CMS's IPPS updates and inflationary pressures on supplies and labor.

The YoY net patient revenue growth of 8.7% stemmed from a balanced mix of volume expansion, favorable case mix improvements, and disciplined pricing strategies. Inpatient revenue, comprising 42% of total net patient revenue, grew 6.8% YoY to $1.20 billion, fueled by a 4.2% increase in adjusted admissions and a 2.5 percentage point rise in our case mix index to 1.92—reflecting higher acuity patients post-COVID, including surges in complex cardiac and oncology cases. Average length of stay held steady at 4.7 days, mitigating some volume pressure from shorter-stay procedures shifting to outpatient settings.

Outpatient revenue, now 55% of our net patient revenue mix—up from 52% last year—was the standout, surging 11.4% YoY to $1.57 billion. This was propelled by a 9.1% rise in outpatient visits to around 925,000 in the quarter, driven by our aggressive expansion into high-margin ambulatory surgery centers, where we added facilities in high-growth Sunbelt markets like Dallas-Fort Worth and Phoenix. Procedures in orthopedics and gastroenterology grew 15% and 12%, respectively, benefiting from partnerships with UnitedHealth Group's Optum for bundled payment models that reduced denial rates by 18% through enhanced prior authorization workflows.

Payer mix played a pivotal role, with commercial and managed care revenue share improving to 48% from 45%, adding about 120 basis points to pricing realization, while Medicare held at 34% amid stable DRG weights. Medicaid dipped slightly to 14% due to targeted deprioritization of low-reimbursement volumes in Midwest markets, offset by stronger performance in expansion states. Bad debt expense as a percentage of gross revenue improved to 2.1% from 2.6%, thanks to our revenue cycle management overhaul powered by AI-driven predictive analytics—reducing days in accounts receivable to 42 from 48.

Shifting to quarter-over-quarter trends, the 2.3% QoQ growth reflects seasonal strength in elective procedures, partially offset by typical summer softness in ED volumes. Inpatient admissions rose 1.8% QoQ, with case mix index expanding 1.1% to capture more bariatric and neuro surgeries. Outpatient momentum accelerated 3.2% QoQ, bolstered by a 5% uptick in telehealth encounters—now 12% of outpatient visits—via our Epic MyChart integration, which has driven patient retention and lowered no-show rates to under 8%. Regionally, our Southeast cluster, representing 45% of net patient revenue, delivered 3.1% QoQ growth on robust volumes in Florida and Texas, where aging demographics and Medicare Advantage penetration mirror national trends. Northeast facilities faced some 0.8% QoQ softness due to Medicaid redeterminations.

Strategically, these results underscore our 'Outpatient First' initiative, shifting 8% of procedural volume from inpatient to lower-cost ambulatory surgery centers and hospital outpatient departments since 2022, enhancing margins by 250 basis points. We're leveraging predictive modeling from our Oracle Health EHR platform to optimize payer contracting—securing 4-6% commercial rate increases in 75% of renewals—and addressing staffing shortages through travel nurse reductions via our internal float pool, now covering 85% of needs. Looking forward, we expect full-year net patient revenue growth of 7-9%, with upside from our ambulatory surgery center pipeline and potential tailwinds from stabilizing out-of-network collections under the No Surprises Act.

Turning now to our core operational metrics: same-facility admissions and patient days, which continue to demonstrate the resilience and growth trajectory of our network. As a reminder, these metrics exclude the impact of our recent tuck-in acquisition of three facilities in the Southeast and the divestiture of an underperforming rural site last year. These figures are normalized for acuity and case mix to provide a clean view of organic performance.

On a year-over-year basis, same-facility admissions grew 4.5% in Q2, accelerating from 3.8% in Q1 and marking our strongest quarterly print since pre-pandemic levels. Quarter-over-quarter, we saw a solid 2.1% uptick from Q1. This performance outpaced the industry average reported by the American Hospital Association, where peers saw closer to 3-4% YoY growth amid payer mix pressures.

This admissions growth was broad-based across service lines. Orthopedics led with 7.2% YoY growth, driven by pent-up demand for total joint replacements and spinal fusions—our elective backlog is now down 85% from COVID peaks, thanks to capacity optimization using predictive analytics from Epic MyChart. Cardiac admissions rose 5.8% YoY, fueled by higher volumes in interventional cardiology and electrophysiology, where we've expanded our TAVR program in partnership with Medtronic, capturing a 15% share increase in Medicare Age+ referrals. Neuroscience grew 4.1%, supported by stroke center designations at 45 facilities, while med-surg baseline held steady at 3.2% amid softer behavioral health volumes due to outpatient diversion.

Patient days tell an even stronger story, up 5.2% YoY and 1.8% QoQ, reflecting not just volume but improved acuity and average length of stay, which expanded 60 basis points YoY to 4.7 days. This stems from a higher case-mix index of 1.82—up 2.3% YoY—driven by complex cases like sepsis, oncology infusions, and post-acute rehab stays. Notably, our observation-to-inpatient conversion rate improved to 28% from 25% a year ago, aided by clinical documentation improvement initiatives with 3M's 360 Encompass CDI software, boosting HCC capture and risk adjustment scores for Medicare Advantage patients.

Regionally, Sunbelt markets—Florida, Texas, and the Carolinas—were standouts, delivering 6.1% YoY admissions growth and 7.0% patient days growth. Florida alone contributed 22% of total admissions, with tailwinds from net migration inflows of over 300,000 seniors annually, boosting demand for joint ventures with Humana and UnitedHealthcare on Medicare Advantage bundled payments. Northeast and Midwest clusters grew more modestly at 2.8% YoY, pressured by nurse staffing ratios and a 5% dip in commercial volumes due to high-deductible health plans. We've mitigated this through our Workforce Command Center, a proprietary AI-driven tool, which reduced agency labor spend by 18% QoQ while maintaining 95% occupancy.

Strategically, these trends underscore our dual-path growth engine: inpatient strength from high-acuity chronic care management—like COPD exacerbations and diabetes-related admissions amid the GLP-1 drug boom—paired with disciplined outpatient migration. We've shifted 12% of low-acuity cases to ambulatory surgery centers, preserving inpatient beds for higher-margin work. Technical initiatives like our statewide tele-ICU rollout with Philips eICU have improved patient throughput by 11%, turning beds 0.3 times faster, while value-based care contracts now cover 42% of admissions, with shared savings from our ACO REACH program exceeding $45 million year-to-date.

Looking forward, we expect Q3 same-facility admissions growth of 4-5% YoY, with patient days at 5-6%, assuming stable CMS IPPS rates and no major respiratory illness resurgence. Risks include payer reimbursement squeezes from No Surprises Act appeals and labor inflation, but our capital investments position us well.

Our operating expenses were $2.45 billion, representing 86% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain efficiencies through our GPO renewals.

Net income for the quarter was $220 million, or $1.10 per diluted share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, a bit more on our capital expenditures for facility modernization and expansion, which totaled $285 million in the quarter, up 28% year-over-year from $222 million. This represents about 22% of our adjusted EBITDA, in line with our 20-25% target range, and positions us for sustained top-line growth.

Approximately 55% of our Q3 CapEx, or $157 million, went toward modernization of existing assets to address aging infrastructure and enhance efficiency amid rising labor costs. Key projects included deploying 12 new Siemens Healthineers Magnetom Free.Max 1.5T MRI systems and eight GE Healthcare Revolution Apex CT scanners across Florida and Texas markets, at a cost of $62 million. These deliver up to 40% faster scan times and 30% lower radiation doses, supporting value-based care under MIPS, with early ROI showing 15% case mix index improvement in pilots.

We invested $45 million in hybrid ORs with Stryker Mako robotic systems and Medtronic Hugo RAS platforms, retrofitting 22 suites in Atlanta and Dallas, boosting same-day discharge rates by 25%. $28 million went to Epic MyChart upgrades with Nuance AI-driven ambient scribing—now live in 18 hospitals—and IoT-enabled patient rooms, reducing no-show rates by 18% in rural sites, with sustainability features targeting 20% energy cost cuts. $22 million for IT backbone refresh, including cybersecurity and our ApexFlow platform, reduced average length of stay by 0.4 days.

Expansions consumed 45% at $128 million, focused on high-growth markets. Sunbelt drove 65%: $75 million for a 120-bed tower at Apex Memorial in Orlando, adding 40 ICU and 80 med-surg beds for Medicare Advantage bundles; $32 million for a 60-bed micro-hospital in suburban Houston via Optum JV; $21 million for three new ASCs in Nashville, Charlotte, and Indianapolis, projected to generate $45 million incremental EBITDA with payback under 24 months.

Sunbelt investments represent 70% of expansion CapEx, fueled by senior migration, delivering 22% CAGR in net patient revenue since 2021. These are gated by 12% IRR minimum and funded 60% from operations, 30% revolver, 10% tax-exempt bonds. We're ahead on our full-year plan, now at $1.15 billion.

As we look ahead, I'm pleased to provide our operating margin guidance, reflecting disciplined execution amid a dynamic landscape. In the just-completed quarter, we delivered 9.2%, up 120 basis points YoY, driven by admissions growth and procedural volumes in orthopedics and cardiovascular—our sixth straight quarter of expansion.

For Q1 next fiscal year, we guide to 9.5% to 10.0%, a sequential improvement. Drivers include 3-4% volume growth, with elective procedures like total knee replacements up 8% via Stryker Mako partnerships; oncology infusions amid rising incidence. Labor discipline targets 52% of revenue, with agency RN usage under 6% via our Talent Pipeline and nursing school partnerships; hours per patient day at 8.2.

Supply chain savings of 2-3% via Vizient GPO and Epic forecasting target $25 million annually. Offsets: 1.5% from CMS IPPS, MA denials at 15% though appeals recovered $18 million. Sunbelt at 11-12% margins with 28% commercial; Northeast 8-9% due to Medicaid and staffing mandates.

For full next fiscal year, 10.0% to 10.8%, toward our 11-13% long-term target. Enablers: Oracle Cerner EHR with 25% doc time reduction; $200 million ASC tuck-ins boosting margins 300 bps; bundled payments for 2% revenue uplift; VBC savings $12 million.

Risks: labor strikes, MA audits, supply disruptions; upside from star ratings.

Finally, on capital expenditures guidance: Through the first half, we've deployed $1.15 billion, guiding full-year 2024 to $1.53 to $1.56 billion. For Q4 2024, $380 to $410 million due to IT and equipment timing.

For fiscal 2025, $1.65 to $1.75 billion, or 5.5-5.8% of revenue. Front-loaded, Q1 at $450-480 million.

Allocation: Facilities/expansions 42% ($700-735M)—$450M for de novos like 120-bed Florida hospital, $180M for eight ASCs, $70M behavioral/LTACH. IT/digital 28% ($460-490M)—$250M EHR/AI, $120M telehealth, $90M cybersecurity/RCM. Equipment/other 30% ($490-525M)—$320M MRI/CT/da Vinci, $120M sustainability, $50M other.

This fuels 200-250 bps margin expansion, prioritizing >15% IRR projects. Southeast 55% spend; risks supply volatility, upside M&A.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Robert Kline:
Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our ACO REACH program has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology like tele-ICU and ambient scribing to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination across our facilities.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Dr. Kline. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the Workforce Command Center on your revenue growth and the impact on hospital efficiency?

Michael Reynolds:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. Our AI-driven Workforce Command Center has been transformative, reducing agency labor spend by 18% quarter-over-quarter while keeping occupancy at 95%. This efficiency has directly supported revenue growth by optimizing staffing for higher patient throughput—turning beds 0.3 times faster—and enabling us to handle the 4.5% admissions surge without proportional cost increases. It's similar to tools at leading systems like Cleveland Clinic, and it's a key factor in our margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

David Patel:
Thanks, Emily. We're prioritizing high-growth Sunbelt markets with $700 million-plus in facilities CapEx next year, including a 120-bed hospital in Florida's Charlotte County and eight new ASCs, adding 15 ORs in Midwest whitespace from rural closures. This targets aging demographics and payer shifts, with projects like our Orlando tower and Houston micro-hospital capturing migration inflows. We expect these to drive 4-6% top-line growth, with payback under three years.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Robert Kline:
Sure, Mike. We're rolling out Philips eICU for tele-ICU statewide, improving throughput by 11%; Epic MyChart with Nuance ambient AI scribing, cutting documentation time 25%; and 3M CDI software for better conversion rates. Our Oracle Health platform optimizes case mix, and telehealth kiosks reduce no-shows by 18%. These integrate with value-based contracts covering 42% of admissions, driving shared savings over $45 million YTD.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wang with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wang:
Thanks. On margin guidance, how are you thinking about labor inflation and supply chain risks?

Jennifer Lee:
Hi, Lisa. Labor remains 52% of revenue target, with agency under 6% via Talent Pipeline. We've got GPO locks for 5% discounts on high-volume items, AI inventory for $25 million savings. Risks like strikes or Red Sea delays are hedged with frame agreements; upside from MA stars and VBC. Confident in 80-100 bps expansion.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Systems Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
